headline: Your phone number can be stolen without anyone touching your phone
summary: SIM swap fraud targets your mobile carrier, allowing attackers to hijack your number and intercept critical security codes, often before you even realize it's happening.
details: SIM swap fraud exploits the weakest link: your mobile carrier. Attackers gather personal details from breaches or social media to impersonate you, then request your number be transferred to their SIM card.
Once transferred, all calls and texts, including one-time verification codes from banks and email providers, are redirected to the attacker. This grants them access to your accounts.

The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) has tracked this since 2018, noting that reported dollar losses understate the true scope. SIM swaps are often just the first step in larger financial frauds.
Unlike many scams, SIM swapping often provides no warning signs to the victim. Many attacks occur without any interaction, with the first indication being a sudden loss of cell signal.
The FBI recommends setting up a PIN or passcode directly with your mobile carrier for account changes. Avoid publicly sharing financial details, crypto holdings, or your phone number on social media.

Furthermore, move away from SMS for security codes where possible, opting for authenticator apps or physical security keys. If you lose signal unexpectedly, contact your carrier immediately from another phone.

headline_marked: [[Agency Agents enables AI to auto-switch expert roles]] for coding, supports Claude Code & Codex
headline: Agency Agents enables AI to auto-switch expert roles for coding, supports Claude Code & Codex
summary: This project offers 230+ specialized AI agent personalities that automatically adapt to coding tasks, eliminating the need for manual prompt engineering. It supports tools like Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI.
details: Tired of manually defining AI roles for coding? The 'Agency Agents' project on GitHub lets AI automatically switch expert personalities, boasting over 143,000 stars. It aims to streamline developer workflows by eliminating repetitive prompt engineering.

Official support includes over 230 specialized AI agent personalities, each with its own professional domain, workflow, and delivery method. It integrates with tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI.

The Agency Agents App acts as a management tool, allowing users to browse available roles and install agents into their preferred coding AI. This simplifies the process of leveraging diverse AI expertise.
Installation is currently available via x64 and ARM64 Windows installers from the GitHub Release page. Users may need to bypass Windows SmartScreen warnings as the current version is not code-signed.

For more proactive AI behavior, users can configure the Agency Agents Router by adding a specific rule to their global CLAUDE.md file. This enables the AI to more actively utilize the specialized agents.
